canDo.en: I can suggest things to do, agree or politely say no, and change an arrangement when something comes up.
canDo.bg: Мога да предлагам какво да правим, да се съглася или учтиво да откажа и да променя уговорка, когато нещо се случи.

title.bg: Предложения, съгласие и промяна на планове

body.en: To suggest, use "How about…" + -ing, "Why don't we…" + verb, or "Shall we…?". To agree, say "Sounds good to me" or "Good idea". To say no politely, start with "I'm afraid…" or "Sorry, I can't make it" — and offer another option if you can. To change a plan, ask "Can we make it a bit later?" or "Shall we leave it till next week?". Careful: after "How about" the verb takes -ing ("How about going"), never "to".
body.bg: За предложение използвай "How about…" + -ing, "Why don't we…" + глагол или "Shall we…?". За съгласие кажи "Sounds good to me" (Звучи ми добре) или "Good idea". За учтив отказ започни с "I'm afraid…" (Съжалявам, но…) или "Sorry, I can't make it" (Няма да мога) — и ако можеш, предложи друг вариант. За да промениш план, питай "Can we make it a bit later?" (Може ли малко по-късно?) или "Shall we leave it till next week?" (Да го оставим за следващата седмица?). Внимавай: след "How about" глаголът е с -ing ("How about going"), никога с "to".

examples: How about going to the cinema on Friday?
Why don't we meet at seven?
I'm afraid I can't make it on Saturday.
Can we make it a bit later?
Shall we leave it till next week?

meaning.en: A place where you go to watch films.
A question word for reasons. "Why don't we…?" is a friendly way to suggest something.
meaning.bg: Защо — въпросителна дума за причина. "Why don't we…?" е приятелски начин да предложиш нещо.

meaning.en: Nice, of high quality, or right for the situation.
To go away from a place; "leave it till…" means to do it later.
meaning.bg: Тръгвам си, оставям; "leave it till…" значи да отложиш нещо за по-късно.

meaning.en: Until; up to a certain time.

objective.en: Suggest an alternative, choose a time that works, and react kindly to a maybe.
objective.bg: Да предложиш друг вариант, да избереш удобен час и да реагираш мило на „може би“.

explanation.en: Good suggestions answer the problem (rain → something indoors) and fit what people have said (Jake is busy till four). "No worries — just let us know" is a relaxed, friendly way to give someone time.
explanation.bg: Доброто предложение решава проблема (дъжд → нещо на закрито) и се съобразява с казаното (Джейк е зает до четири). "No worries — just let us know" е спокоен, приятелски начин да дадеш на някого време.

hints.en: Remember what Jake says about football.
hints.bg: Запомни какво казва Джейк за футбола.

scene.en: You're on a video call with your friends Priya and Jake, planning Saturday.
scene.bg: На видеоразговор си с приятелите си Прия и Джейк и планирате събота.

lines.text: So, what are we doing on Saturday? Any ideas?
We could go hiking, but the forecast says it might rain all day.

options.text: How about that new escape room in town instead? It's indoors.
How about to go to the escape room?

why.en: After "How about" use -ing: "How about going…?" — or just a noun: "How about the escape room?"
why.bg: След "How about" идва -ing: "How about going…?" — или направо съществително: "How about the escape room?"

why.en: It's "I agree" (no "am"). And hiking in the rain isn't a great plan — Jake just said that.
why.bg: Казва се "I agree" (без "am"). А и разходка в планината в дъжда не е добър план — Джейк точно това каза.

lines.text: Ooh, good idea. I've heard it's really fun. What time works for everyone?
I've got football till four, so anything after five is fine for me.

options.text: Shall we say six, then? We could grab a pizza afterwards.

why.en: Jake is playing football until four, so three won't work for him.
why.bg: Джейк играе футбол до четири, така че три часа не му е удобно.

options.text: Let's meet at six o'clock, isn't it?

why.en: "Isn't it" doesn't fit here. To check, say "Shall we say six?" or "Six OK?"
why.bg: "Isn't it" не пасва тук. За да провериш, кажи "Shall we say six?" или "Six OK?"

lines.text: Perfect. I'll book it for six.
Actually, hang on — my sister's birthday dinner might be on Saturday. Can I let you know tomorrow?

options.text: No worries — just let us know by tomorrow evening.

why.en: Too pushy for friends — he's just told you why he can't answer yet.
why.bg: Твърде настойчиво за приятели — той току-що обясни защо още не може да отговори.

options.text: Don't worry, we'll go without you then.

why.en: This sounds like you don't care if he comes. Give him time to decide.
why.bg: Звучи така, сякаш не те интересува дали ще дойде. Дай му време да реши.

objective.en: Apologise for being late, suggest a new time and confirm who does what.
objective.bg: Да се извиниш за закъснение, да предложиш нов час и да потвърдиш кой какво ще направи.

explanation.en: Use "be going to" for something you can already see coming ("I'm going to be late"). "Would seven thirty work for you?" is a friendly way to suggest a new time. Listen for who is changing the booking — Chris offers to do it.
explanation.bg: Използвай "be going to" за нещо, което вече виждаш, че ще стане ("I'm going to be late"). "Would seven thirty work for you?" е приятелски начин да предложиш нов час. Слушай кой ще промени резервацията — Крис предлага той да го направи.

hints.en: In the last turn, remember who is calling the restaurant.
hints.bg: В последната реплика помни кой ще се обади в ресторанта.

scene.en: You're meeting Chris for dinner at seven, but your train is late. He calls you.
scene.bg: Имаш среща с Крис за вечеря в седем, но влакът ти закъснява. Той ти звъни.

lines.text: Hey! Are you on your way?

options.text: Sort of — I'm really sorry, but my train's been delayed. I'm going to be about half an hour late.
Yes, I come in half an hour.

why.en: Use "I'll be there" or "I'm going to be late". "I come" sounds like a habit, not this evening.
why.bg: Кажи "I'll be there" или "I'm going to be late". "I come" звучи като навик, а не като тази вечер.

options.text: Sorry, I will be late since half an hour.

why.en: "Since" is for a starting point in the past. Say "about half an hour late".
why.bg: "Since" е за начален момент в миналото. Кажи "about half an hour late".

lines.text: Oh no! Don't worry. Do you want to meet a bit later, then?

options.text: Would seven thirty work for you instead?
Would seven thirty works for you instead?

why.en: After "would", use the base form: "work", not "works".
why.bg: След "would" глаголът е в основна форма: "work", а не "works".

options.text: Could we cancel it for seven thirty?

why.en: "Cancel" means the dinner won't happen at all. You want to move it: "Could we make it seven thirty?"
why.bg: "Cancel" значи вечерята изобщо да не се състои. Ти искаш да я преместиш: "Could we make it seven thirty?"

lines.text: Seven thirty's fine. I'll call the restaurant and change the booking.

options.text: Brilliant, thanks for being so understanding. See you then!
OK, I'll change the booking, then.

why.en: Chris just said HE will call the restaurant. Thank him instead.
why.bg: Крис току-що каза, че ТОЙ ще се обади в ресторанта. По-добре му благодари.

options.text: Thanks, see you on seven thirty!

why.en: With clock times, use "at": "See you at seven thirty!"
why.bg: С часове се използва "at": "See you at seven thirty!"

objective.en: Understand a change of plan in a voicemail.
objective.bg: Да разбереш промяна в плана от гласово съобщение.

explanation.en: Zoe cancels the picnic because of the weather ("the picnic's off") and says "I've booked a table for one o'clock" at an Italian restaurant.
explanation.bg: Зоуи отменя пикника заради времето ("the picnic's off" — пикникът отпада) и казва "I've booked a table for one o'clock" (запазила е маса за един часа) в италиански ресторант.

hints.en: "The picnic's off" means it's cancelled. What does she do instead?
hints.bg: "The picnic's off" значи, че е отменен. Какво прави тя вместо това?

items.audio: Hi, it's Zoe. Listen, about Sunday — the weather looks awful, so the picnic's off. Why don't we all go to that Italian place by the river instead? I've booked a table for one o'clock, but if that's too early for anyone, just text me and I'll move it. Bye!
items.question: What has Zoe done?
options: She's booked a table for lunch on Sunday.
She's cancelled lunch because of the weather.
She's moved the picnic to one o'clock.
She's asked everyone to book a table.

objective.en: Follow a conversation where the time changes twice.
objective.bg: Да следиш разговор, в който часът се сменя два пъти.

explanation.en: Eight becomes nine, but nine doesn't work for Ryan, so they move to the evening: "let's do six, then".
explanation.bg: Осем става девет, но девет не е удобно за Райън, затова местят тренировката вечерта: "let's do six, then" (тогава в шест).

hints.en: Only the last time they agree on counts.
hints.bg: Важи само последният час, за който се разбират.

items.audio:
Ryan: Are we still on for the gym tomorrow at eight?
Laura: Actually, could we make it nine? I've got a dentist appointment first.
Ryan: Nine's a bit tricky — I start work at ten. What about the evening instead?
Laura: Fine by me. Let's do six, then.
items.question: When are they going to the gym?
options: Tomorrow at eight in the morning
Tomorrow at nine in the morning
Tomorrow at six in the evening

objective.en: Repeat a polite refusal with an alternative.
objective.bg: Да повториш учтив отказ с друго предложение.

explanation.en: "I'm afraid I can't make it" softens the "no", and offering another day keeps the plan alive.
explanation.bg: "I'm afraid I can't make it" смекчава отказа, а предложението за друг ден запазва плана.

hints.en: "Can't make it" sounds like one word: "cantmakeit".
hints.bg: "Can't make it" звучи почти като една дума.

items.prompt: I'm afraid I can't make it tonight — can we do Thursday instead?
items.model: I'm afraid I can't make it tonight — can we do Thursday instead?
items.target: I'm afraid I can't make it tonight — can we do Thursday instead?

explanation.en: "Why don't we…?" + a reason ("That way…") makes a suggestion sound friendly and thought through.
explanation.bg: "Why don't we…?" + причина ("That way…" — така…) прави предложението приятелско и обмислено.

hints.en: Let your voice go down at the end of "Why don't we…?" — it's a suggestion, not a real question.
hints.bg: Гласът ти слиза в края на "Why don't we…?" — това е предложение, а не истински въпрос.

items.prompt: Why don't we meet outside the cinema at quarter to eight? That way we'll have time to get popcorn.
items.model: Why don't we meet outside the cinema at quarter to eight? That way we'll have time to get popcorn.
items.target: Why don't we meet outside the cinema at quarter to eight? That way we'll have time to get popcorn.

explanation.en: A good answer has three parts: say sorry, give a short reason, and (if you can) suggest another time.
explanation.bg: Добрият отговор има три части: извинение, кратка причина и (ако можеш) друг вариант.

items.prompt: Your friend says: "Do you want to come to a concert on Saturday?" You're busy. What do you say?
items.model: Sorry, I can't make it on Saturday — I'm working. How about next weekend?

explanation.en: "About" is a preposition, and after prepositions English uses the -ing form: "How about meeting…?" (or "What about meeting…?").
explanation.bg: "About" е предлог, а след предлози в английския глаголът е с -ing: "How about meeting…?" (или "What about meeting…?").

hints.en: What form of the verb comes after "about"?
hints.bg: Каква форма на глагола идва след "about"?

items.sentence: How about to meet at the station at six?
accept: How about meeting at the station at six?
What about meeting at the station at six?
